html:
Roman writer, officer and naturalist, author of the Natural History, an encyclopedia of the ancient world.

Born at Novum Comum (Como) in northern Italy, he served as a cavalry officer on the German frontier and wrote a history of Rome's German wars, now lost. Under his friend Vespasian he held high posts, and he finished as admiral of the fleet at Misenum, on the Bay of Naples. He worked without stop; his nephew says he had books read to him while he ate and bathed.

In August 79 CE he saw a huge cloud rise over Vesuvius. He sailed across the bay to look and to rescue friends, and landed at Stabiae. The next day he died on the beach, probably from the fumes or a heart attack (see Vesuvius buries Pompeii).

We know the story from two letters his nephew Pliny the Younger wrote to the historian Tacitus. His Natural History, dedicated to Titus, stayed a standard reference into the Renaissance.
sum: Roman writer, officer and naturalist, author of the Natural History, an encyclopedia of the ancient world.
